transit.name: Black Hawk & Central City Tramway
transit.detail: Free shuttle; the Central City route links three stops in town with Black Hawk. Runs from 10 am to 2 am Monday to Thursday and to 3 am Friday to Sunday, every 20 to 30 minutes.

nameOrigin.text: William Newton Byers, founder of the Rocky Mountain News, reportedly named the town for its central location in the mining district.

founded.text: John Gregory discovered lode gold on May 6, 1859, in a gulch between what became Black Hawk and Central City.

timeline.text: The Teller House hotel was built.
Fire destroyed all but one of the buildings on Main Street.
The Opera House held its grand opening.
The Central City-Black Hawk Historic District was designated a National Historic Landmark on July 4.

sites.name: Central City Opera House
sites.hours: Tours from the Washington Hall Tour Office, 117 Eureka St.: daily 10 am to 4 pm Memorial Day weekend through September; Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 4 pm the rest of the year
sites.cost: Tours $10 per person per building; children 12 and under free

sites.name: Gilpin History Museum
sites.hours: Daily 10 am to 4 pm, Memorial Day weekend through the end of September
sites.season: Closed for the winter; access by appointment or through the Tour Office
